props.name: caption

props.doc: Dim the marks outside the focused element, as a click highlight does. Defaults to true.
props.name: emphasis

props.doc: The most data fields read out for one mark. Defaults to 8.
props.name: maxFields

props.doc: The chart parts the walk reaches, in reading order. Defaults to every section.
props.name: sections

props.doc: How far neighbouring wedges stand apart, in px.
props.name: gap

props.doc: `rule` paints the shared edge; `pad` swings the wedges apart.
props.name: gapStyle

props.doc: The hole as a share of the outer radius, 0–0.9, for every donut the house draws.
props.name: hole

props.doc:
The order wedges run clockwise from the start (M4): the data's order (default), or largest
first. A chart that sorts its own slices keeps its sort.
props.name: order

props.doc: Where the first wedge starts, in degrees clockwise from 12 o'clock (default 0).
props.name: startAngle

props.doc: The line along the top of the fill: an area that keeps its edge reads as a line with a wash.
props.name: edge

props.doc:
`fade` runs the fill from the area's ink at its top to clear at the baseline. Stacked bands
keep a solid fill: each sits on the next, and a fade would melt one into the other.
props.name: fill

props.doc: Whether to add tooltips to the chart (default: false)
props.name: addTooltips

props.doc: The range's spread either side of its centre, as a ratio: unset, the stretch allowed.
props.name: aspectTolerance

props.doc:
Whether to auto-wrap column-only facets into a 2D grid.

When `true` (default), `computeFacetGrid` considers wrapping N
column facets into multiple rows, choosing the layout whose
overall aspect ratio best matches the canvas AR.

When `false`, column-only facets stay in a single row (capped
at the maximum that fits the canvas budget). Useful for small
multiples that should always be side-by-side.
props.name: autoFacetWrap

props.doc:
Whether a plot with one banded axis leans back where its bands, with the labels it cannot
drop, put it outside the shapes a chart of its base takes on its own (default true). That
range runs from the base with its height stretched to the base with its width stretched
(at least 1.25× either side); where it cannot be reached readably, a range half as wide
again is aimed for instead.
props.name: bandBalance

props.doc:
Blend between the scaled base band and the available span per item.

 baseSpanStep = baseSpan / N
 capacityStep = availableCapacity / N
 preferredStep = baseSpanStep > baseStep
     ? baseStep × (1 − fit) + capacityStep × fit
     : baseStep

`0` gives fixed-step behavior (Vega-Lite); `1` aims toward the available
canvas capacity on sparse axes (ECharts, Chart.js, Plotly). The selected
pitch then passes through normal elastic stretch/compression. Two-banded
cell grids bypass this policy. Default: 0.
props.name: bandStepFit

props.doc: Explicit X-axis capacity for sparse band fitting. Internal assembler bridge.
props.name: bandStepFitCapacityX

props.doc: Explicit Y-axis capacity for sparse band fitting. Internal assembler bridge.
props.name: bandStepFitCapacityY

props.doc:
Backend-native base font size (px) for axis **tick labels**, at a 300px
reference canvas. The core scales it subtly with canvas size and uses it
as the ceiling of the shrink→rotate→cap ladder, so a chart never renders
ticks below its backend's native scale on a comfortable canvas.

Learned from each renderer's defaults:
  - Vega-Lite: 10   - ECharts: 12   - Chart.js: 12   - Plotly: 12

Default: 10.
props.name: baseLabelFontSize

props.doc:
Backend-native base font size (px) for **headers** (axis titles, legend,
chart title), at a 300px reference canvas. Scaled subtly with canvas size
(grows up to +4 on large canvases, shrinks toward the base in small
multiples) so headers stay proportionate to the chart.

Learned from each renderer's defaults:
  - Vega-Lite: 11   - ECharts: 12   - Chart.js: 12   - Plotly: 14

Default: 11.
props.name: baseTitleFontSize

props.doc:
What the layout does when the chart will not read well in its canvas: the title, keys, labels
and chrome taking the chart area's room, the drawing overflowing its box past legibility, or
stretched out of its box's shape. `'auto'` (the default) lays such a chart out again — each part
given a box from the canvas and fitted to it (keys on the edge with room, their names wrapped;
the title set down to fit), then, where that is not enough, cheap treatments one at a time — and
keeps the cheapest that reads well. A chart that reads well as planned is never changed.
`'off'` lays every chart out as planned.
props.name: canvasFit

props.doc:
Whether the canvas fit, once it has settled what is around the chart, lays the plot out once
more in the room the box leaves it — kept only where the chart reads better for it (default true).
props.name: canvasRefit

props.doc: Internal: the treatment a canvas-fit pass lays the chart out under.
props.name: canvasTreatment

props.doc:
How far a grid's cells grow past their reading target (28 px) toward the size that fills the
base, from 0 (not at all, the default) to 1 (to twice the target at most). Set from a house's
`layout.bandStepFit`.
props.name: cellGrowth

props.doc:
Gas-pressure tuning for continuous axes (default: scatter-plot settings).
- A single number overrides markCrossSection (σ) for both axes.
- An object allows per-axis σ plus optional elasticity / maxStretch:
  `{ x: 100, y: 0, elasticity: 0.7, maxStretch: 2 }`
  x/y = 0 means "don't stretch this axis".
  Useful for line/area charts where horizontal crowding matters
  far more than vertical.
props.name: continuousMarkCrossSection

props.doc: Per-axis stretch elasticity (default: 0.3). Higher → more responsive.
props.name: elasticity

props.doc: Per-axis stretch cap (default: 1.5).
props.name: maxStretch

props.doc:
Which axis uses series-count-based pressure instead of pixel counting.
- 'x' or 'y': that axis uses nSeries × σ / dim for pressure.
- 'auto': auto-detect — in 2D (both continuous), defaults to 'y';
  in 1D (one continuous + one discrete), uses the continuous axis.
The σ for the series axis is used directly (not sqrt'd) since series
count is inherently 1D.
props.name: seriesCountAxis

props.doc:
Base pixels per discrete category at a 300px baseline canvas.
Scaled proportionally with canvas size by the core layout engine.
The final default step size is:

  defaultStepSize = defaultBandSize × max(1, canvasSize/300)

Backends set this to match their native bar/band rendering:
  - VL:  ~20 (VL uses width:{step:N} which auto-sizes the plot area)
  - EC:  ~20 (ECharts adds generous grid margins)
  - CJS: ~30 (Chart.js fills the canvas; wider bands look more native)

Templates can override via paramOverrides for chart types that need
more space per band (e.g. jitter: 40, funnel: 50, sankey: 60).

Default: 20.
props.name: defaultBandSize

props.doc: Power-law exponent for discrete axis stretch (default: 0.5)
props.name: elasticity

props.doc:
Resistance to aspect-ratio distortion when faceting.

When faceting divides one dimension (e.g. width by column count),
the subplot aspect ratio drifts away from the single-plot ratio.
Line and area charts are very sensitive to this because their
visual signal is encoded in slopes and curve shapes.

This parameter partially compensates by shrinking the undivided
dimension so the panel aspect ratio stays closer to the original:

  arDrift = facetedAR / baseAR          (< 1 when panel is narrower)
  correctedDim = dim × arDrift ^ resistance

- 0 (default): no correction — current behavior.
- 0.3–0.5: moderate resistance (recommended for line / area).
- 1: fully preserve the single-plot aspect ratio.
props.name: facetAspectRatioResistance

props.doc:
Explicit number of facet COLUMNS for a column-wrapped facet, overriding
the auto-computed wrap. When set (≥ 1) the layout uses this many columns
(clamped to the distinct column count) and wraps the remaining panels
into as many rows as needed. Surfaced to hosts as the `facetColumns`
chart property so users can dial the wrap in interactively; undefined =
auto (fill the width).
props.name: facetColumns

props.doc: Power-law exponent for facet subplot stretch — lower = more conservative (default: 0.3)
props.name: facetElasticity

props.doc:
Fixed overhead in px for axis labels, titles, legend, etc.
Subtracted once from the total canvas budget (not per-panel).
Each backend sets its own default; core uses { width: 0, height: 0 }.
props.name: facetFixedPadding

props.doc:
Gap in px between adjacent facet panels (spacing, headers).
Used directly by the core layout engine to compute subplot sizes
and max canvas dimensions.
Each backend sets its own value (VL ≈ 10, ECharts ≈ 14); core uses 0.
props.name: facetGap

props.doc: The gap between facet columns and between facet rows the panels are laid out for, where it differs from `facetGap`; set by the plan.
props.name: facetGapColumn

props.doc:
When a discrete axis is **grouped** (dodged lanes within each category
band), by default the band's elastic stretch target is the *per-item*
step — so a category holding N lanes is only sized as if it held one.
For thin marks (grouped bars) that's fine: 4 lanes share a ~66px band
comfortably. But wide marks — a box-and-whisker glyph — need real room
per lane, and the per-item target leaves grouped boxplots compressed on
an otherwise roomy canvas.

When set, the grouped band instead targets `itemsPerGroup × step`, so
the category band stretches to give each lane its full width (still
bounded by `maxBandSize × itemsPerGroup` and the canvas budget). Scoped
to templates whose grouped glyph is wide (boxplot); left off for bars so
their tuned grouped spacing does not change.
props.name: groupBandFillsLanes

props.doc:
The smallest band step (per group where bars are grouped) the value labels need on each axis,
which the plan has checked the canvas can hold. Internal: the plan sets it when it widens the
bands for their labels.
props.name: labelStep

props.doc:
Set by the interactive renderer when a viewport will change the rows in view:
value labels are built for any window that could print them, and this signal
decides whether they show.
props.name: liveLayoutSignal

props.doc:
When true, continuous X and Y axes stretch together using the
larger of the two per-axis stretch factors. This preserves the
aspect ratio of the data space. (default: false — axes stretch
independently based on their own density.)
props.name: maintainContinuousAxisRatio

props.doc:
Maximum pixels per discrete category at a 300px baseline canvas,
scaled proportionally with canvas size (like {@link defaultBandSize}).

This is the **sparse-expansion ceiling**. When few categories share a
wide plot, each band grows to fill the available width but never past
`maxBandSize`, so one or two bars can't balloon to the whole canvas.
The band is thus clamped to `[minStep, maxBandSize]`:

  step = clamp(availableWidth / N, minStep, maxBandSize)

Backends set this to match their native sparse-bar rendering:
  - VL:  = defaultBandSize (VL's step-based sizing doesn't fill a container)
  - EC / CJS / Plotly: much larger (these fill their plot area natively)

Defaults to {@link defaultBandSize} (no expansion beyond the base band).
props.name: maxBandSize

props.doc: Maximum number of distinct color values before overflow truncation (default: 24)
props.name: maxColorValues

props.doc:
Default maximum stretch multiplier used when the spec provides no
explicit `canvasSize` ceiling (default: 2).

This is a **unified** budget: the combined stretch from facet
layout AND discrete/banded axis sizing must stay within this
factor.  For example, with maxStretch=2 and a 400px base,
the total chart width never exceeds 800px regardless of how
many facet columns or discrete axis items there are.

When `chart_spec.canvasSize` IS set, the per-dimension caps
`maxStretchX`/`maxStretchY` are derived from `canvasSize / baseSize`
instead and this scalar is ignored.
props.name: maxStretch

props.doc:
Resolved per-dimension stretch cap for the X (width) axis.

Normally derived by the assembler from `canvasSize / baseSize`
(or `maxStretch` when no ceiling is set). Callers rarely set this
directly. Falls back to `maxStretch` when absent.
props.name: maxStretchX

props.doc:
Resolved per-dimension stretch cap for the Y (height) axis.

Normally derived by the assembler from `canvasSize / baseSize`
(or `maxStretch` when no ceiling is set). Callers rarely set this
directly. Falls back to `maxStretch` when absent.
props.name: maxStretchY

props.doc:
Chart-specific **floor** on the per-category band step (at a 300px
baseline canvas), which a house's `layout.bandStep` may grow but not
undercut. Ordinary charts have no such floor: a compact house is right
to print thin bars. But a few chart types are only legible above a
minimum band width regardless of house — a slopegraph draws its whole
meaning from the angle of two columns, and a house that packs them 46px
apart turns every slope near-vertical and leaves no room for the end
labels. Such a template states the width its read needs here, and the
house is held to it as a minimum while still free to spread wider.

Unset for most templates (no floor). Set via paramOverrides.
props.name: minBandStep

props.doc:
The smallest axis tick label (px) the shrink ladder may reach, as small multiples
shrink their plots. A themed chart takes its theme's `type.minSize`. Default: 6.
props.name: minLabelFontSize

props.doc: Minimum pixels per discrete axis item (default: 6)
props.name: minStep

props.doc: Minimum facet subplot size in px (default: 60)
props.name: minSubplotSize

props.doc:
Internal: the names down y stand on their own line above each bar. The y band starts at
`scale` times the house band, never under `scale` times the least step nor `minStep` — a
name's line, its bar and the air between — by the same stretch.
props.name: rowNamesAbove

props.doc:
Fraction of each step reserved for inter-category padding (0–1).
VL pads *inside* the step (band = step × (1 − padding)), so this
value should match VL's paddingInner.  ECharts pads *outside* the
band, so the layout engine passes this through so ECharts can
compute barWidth = step × (1 − stepPadding) explicitly.

Default: 0.1 (matching VL's default band paddingInner).
props.name: stepPadding

props.doc: The centre of that range, as width over height: unset, the base's.
props.name: targetAspect

props.doc:
Target aspect ratio for a single band (step height ÷ step width).

When a banded (discrete) axis is opposite a continuous axis, each
band has a natural AR = continuousAxisSize / stepSize.  If that
exceeds the target, the continuous axis is shrunk via a log-space
blend so bands don't become excessively tall/wide.

- `undefined` / 0: no band-AR correction.
- Typical values: 8–15 (VL default ≈ 10, ECharts ≈ 12).

Only affects charts with exactly one banded axis and one
continuous axis (e.g. bar, lollipop).  Has no effect on
scatter, line, or fully-banded charts.
props.name: targetBandAR

props.doc: Attach the theme's resolved decisions to the spec as `_theme.decisions`, for tools that inspect them. Default: false.
props.name: themeDecisions

props.doc: Hard override for eligible preset distances, in renderer pixels.
props.name: maxDistance

props.doc: Limits the preset to one axis; both discrete axes when unset.
props.name: axis

props.doc: Defaults to 'click'.
props.name: event

props.doc: Gestures that return this interaction to its neutral state.
props.name: reset

props.doc: The rule's and ticks' own ink, in place of `ink.structure.axis`; the presence still tones it (AX1).
props.name: color

props.doc:
Distance from the axis rule to its labels in px. For outward ticks, the
tick occupies the first part of this distance.
props.name: labelGap

props.doc: Stroke width of the axis rule in px. Presence still decides whether it is drawn.
props.name: lineWeight
placement

props.doc:
Drop the axis entirely when every mark already prints its own value.
The scale is then carried by the numbers, not by a ruler beside them.
Mirrors `legend.suppressWhenValuesPrinted`.
props.name: suppressWhenValuesPrinted

props.doc:
How finely a *measure* ruler is graduated: one gradation per 60 / 45 / 30px
of axis, floored at three. A hint — the renderer still rounds to its own
1/2/5/10 step, so a dense ask on a short axis can land on half units.
props.name: tickDensity

props.doc: Rounding at the *value* end only, so a stack still reads as one column.
props.name: cornerRadius

props.doc: How much of its step the bar fills, 0–1. The rest is the gap.
props.name: fraction

props.doc:
Grouped (dodged) bars: `gap` between the bars in a group and `spacing` between groups, each a
share of a bar's width (`0` touching, `1` a bar's width) or px (`"2px"`); the bars take what is
left of the step: the bar's width is derived, and the step is a guideline. Unset `spacing`
keeps `fraction` for the group as a whole, but never less than half a bar or three gaps, so
groups read as groups; unset `gap` is a twentieth of a bar, at least 1px.
props.name: group

props.doc:
The least length, px, a bar with a non-zero value is drawn (M6): a near-zero bar shows as a
stub at the baseline rather than vanishing into it. Zero stays empty.
props.name: minLength

props.doc: The ink of the outline: the structure ink (default), the surface, or each bar's own series ink.
props.name: outlineInk

props.doc: Defaults to 'xy'.
props.name: axes

props.doc: Returns the viewport to the full frame. Defaults to ['double-click', 'escape'].
props.name: reset

props.doc: The flight home on reset. Defaults to 400 ms; `{ duration: 0 }` jumps.
props.name: resetTransition

props.doc: The zoom into the brushed region. Defaults to 400 ms; `{ duration: 0 }` jumps.
props.name: transition

CanvasTreatment.doc:
A treatment the canvas-fit pass lays a chart out under, to win back room the title, keys and
names took from the chart area (see `AssembleOptions.canvasFit`).

props.doc: Every key at one edge: beside the plot, or in one row above or below it.
props.name: keys

props.doc: Long key names kept to this many px a column, wrapped onto lines before they are cut.
props.name: names

props.doc:
One key moved to another edge, the others left where they stand: the key at `index` among
the chart's keys. `title` names it, for reports.
props.name: oneKey

props.doc:
The plot laid out at this share of its base size, both ways, so it keeps its shape: what the
box cannot hold comes out of the plot rather than out of every glyph, as a host shrinking the
whole drawing would take it.
props.name: plotScale

props.doc:
The room the box leaves the plot once what is around the chart is settled, in px: the plot is
laid out again in it, once. A continuous side takes it; a banded side keeps its steps.
props.name: plotSpace

props.doc:
The width the names down the y axis are given, in px: longer ones wrap onto a second line, so
the chart area — its plot and its names — takes the width the box leaves it.
props.name: rowNames

props.doc: The headline and deck set at this share of their size, never below a legible floor.
props.name: titleScale

props.doc: Cut between tiles, in px. Zero keeps the grid a continuous field.
props.name: gap

props.doc: Chart specification — describes *what* to draw.
props.name: chart_spec

props.doc:
Base (target) chart size in pixels — the size layout aims for when the
data fits comfortably (default: `{ width: 400, height: 320 }`).

For faceted charts this is the whole-chart target; panels divide it.
The chart may grow beyond `baseSize` under pressure (dense axes, many
facet panels), bounded by `canvasSize`.
props.name: baseSize

props.doc:
Hard ceiling on the rendered size in pixels (optional).

The final image — a single plot OR an entire facet grid — never exceeds
this box. The per-dimension growth allowance is derived from the ratio
to `baseSize`: `βx = canvasSize.width / baseSize.width`,
`βy = canvasSize.height / baseSize.height` (each clamped to ≥ 1).

When omitted, the ceiling defaults to `baseSize × options.maxStretch`
(default 1.5×) in each dimension.
props.name: canvasSize

props.doc: Template-specific configurable properties (e.g., bar corner radius, show labels)
props.name: chartProperties

props.doc: Template name, e.g. `"Scatter Plot"`, `"Bar Chart"`
props.name: chartType

props.doc:
The house chrome this chart keeps. Unset follows the theme. `false` drops it all; an object
turns off parts: `header` (rules, tabs, wordmarks and logos above or beside the title),
`footer` (the closing rule and the house's credit beside the source) and `logos` (every
logo, header or footer — a footer credit then shows its words). The source line itself is
drawn whenever `source` is given.
props.name: chrome

props.doc:
Channel → encoding map (e.g., `{ x: { field: 'weight' }, y: { field: 'mpg' } }`).
A bare string is shorthand for `{ field: <string> }` (e.g. `{ x: 'weight' }`).
props.name: encodings

props.doc:
A short line above the headline: a figure label (“Figure 2”) or a kicker. Set in the
theme's `type.kicker`.
props.name: label

props.doc:
Where the data comes from, drawn as the chart's source line in the house's way (the theme's
`source`). Optional: give it only where the source is known — an agent should not invent one.
props.name: source

props.doc: The deck: the reading of the headline — what is measured, of whom, when, in what units.
props.name: subtitle

props.doc:
The headline — what this chart says, in words.

Themes that omit required axis titles append their names and units
to the subtitle instead. The compiler does not interpret this text
to decide whether it explains an axis.
props.name: title

props.doc:
Data source — either inline rows or a reference the host can resolve.

 - `{ values: any[] }` — an array of row objects (like Vega-Lite `data.values`).
- `{ url: string }`   — a URL or path reference to JSON/CSV data.
  Hosts that need local semantic/layout decisions should resolve this to
  rows before assembly. The MCP renderer reads local JSON/CSV/TSV
  files referenced by path; it does not fetch remote URLs.

 At least one of `values` or `url` must be provided.
props.name: data

props.doc:
Localized display names for fields (column name → display label).
When present, used as axis titles and legend headers instead of raw field names.
props.name: field_display_names

props.doc:
Interactions — describes *how it behaves*.

Presets named by type with their options, each with its own reset
gestures, and the targeting policies. Retained state is not part of it;
a host applies that through the interactive surface.
Sits beside `chart_spec` for the same reason `theme_spec`
does: one behaviour applies to many charts, and a static backend ignores
it without harm.

Read by the interactive surface in `flint-chart/interactive` (Vega-Lite
only). The assemblers leave it untouched. A preset the chart cannot
honour is dropped with a warning rather than failing the chart.
props.name: interaction_spec

props.doc:
Options for the assembler — layout tuning, tooltips, etc.
All fields are optional and have sensible defaults.
props.name: options

props.doc:
Per-column semantic type annotations.

Maps field names to semantic type strings (e.g., `"Quantity"`, `"Country"`,
`"Year"`, `"Percentage"`). These drive encoding type resolution, zero-baseline
decisions, color schemes, formatting, and more.

Fields not listed here fall back to `inferVisCategory()` which inspects
raw data values.
props.name: semantic_types

props.doc:
Theme — describes *how it should look*.

Either the name of a house Flint ships (`'economist'`, `'nature'`, …see
`listThemePresets()`), a `ThemeSpec` of your own, or a `ThemeSpec` that
`extends` a shipped house and overrides selected fields. A ThemeSpec is a
portable design language (ink, type, structure, marks, chrome policy),
stated without ever naming a channel, field, or backend property. The
compiler grounds it against this chart and then realizes it in the
target backend.

Sits beside `chart_spec` rather than inside it because the same theme
applies to every chart and the same chart accepts any theme — nesting it
would make that independence unstatable.

Currently realized by the Vega-Lite assembler only. Other assemblers
accept the shared input field but do not apply it.
props.name: theme_spec

ChartEncoding.doc:
Encoding definition for a single channel, using field names directly.
This is the library-level encoding — no fieldID indirection.

props.doc: Colour channel: quantize a continuous measure into this many bins; `0` keeps the ramp continuous.
props.name: bins

props.doc: Colour channel: colours bound to values, for this chart (the field's `colors`): `{ "Win": "#2a9d8f" }`.
props.name: colors

props.doc: Colour channel: the measure extent the ramp spans, `[low, high]`, in place of the data's.
props.name: domain

props.doc: Colour channel: the value a diverging scale pivots on, for this chart (the field's `divergingMidpoint`).
props.name: mid

props.doc: Colour channel: run the scale the other way round.
props.name: reverse

props.doc:
Colour channel: a Vega scheme name (`viridis`, `redblue`), or the stops a ramp or palette runs

The name the channel's axis or key prints, in place of the field's; `null` prints none. A

Base (target) chart size in pixels — the size layout aims for when the
data fits comfortably (default: `{ width: 400, height: 320 }`).

For faceted charts this is the whole-chart target; panels divide it.
The chart may grow beyond `baseSize` under pressure (dense axes, many
facet panels), bounded by `canvasSize`.

props.doc:
Hard ceiling on the rendered size in pixels (optional).

The final image — a single plot OR an entire facet grid — never exceeds
this box. The per-dimension growth allowance is derived from the ratio
to `baseSize`: `βx = canvasSize.width / baseSize.width`,
`βy = canvasSize.height / baseSize.height` (each clamped to ≥ 1).

When omitted, the ceiling defaults to `baseSize × options.maxStretch`
(default 1.5×) in each dimension.

The options each preset type accepts in a spec. They are the factory option

Which lines keep the dots (M5): `countable` (default) — lines of up to 12 readings; `all` —
every line, the dots shrinking to fit; `sparse` — only where readings stand 20px apart or more.

A ring in the plot's colour around each dot, so overlapping dots stay countable. A line's dots
get one wherever lines can cross unless this says `omit`; a scatter's dots only where it is
declared. A quarter of the dot's radius, at most `width`; a scatter's dots under 28px² get
none. An outline takes its place. Not combined with an `opacity` below 1: ringed dots are solid.
props.name: halo

so overlaps show through. A house whose marks are flat planes states 1. Dots a full plot shrinks

`opacity` property still wins.

SemanticAnnotation.doc: Enriched semantic annotation from LLM or user.

props.doc:
Colours bound to values of this field, wherever they fall: `{ "DFL": "#0793AB" }`. Matched on
the value, trimmed and case-insensitive. Values left out take the palette in order, which then
skips the bound colours. Wins over the theme's role inks.
props.name: colors

props.doc:
The value a diverging colour scale should pivot on — what the reader is
being asked to compare against.

This is a judgement, not a fact about the field, which is why it has to
be declared rather than inferred. A temperature in °C pivots at 0 if the
question is whether it freezes, and at something nearer 18 if the
question is whether a city is comfortable to live in; the numbers are
identical either way and only the question tells them apart. Declare it
when the chart is about the comparison — above and below an average, a
target, a baseline period, a comfort line — and leave it out otherwise,
in which case the pivot falls back to whatever the type and the data
make obvious: a sign change at zero, a bounded domain's centre, or no
pivot at all.

Declaring one also *asserts* the split: the scale diverges even if every
reading happens to land on one side of it.
props.name: divergingMidpoint

props.doc:
Intrinsic domain (value range) of this field's scale.
Only for bounded/scaled types — NOT for open-ended measures.
E.g., [1, 5] for 5-star rating, [0, 100] for score, [-90, 90] for latitude.
props.name: intrinsicDomain

props.doc:
Which way the field's values are good, for a diverging colour: `higher-is-better` (profit,
growth) puts the warm, alarming end on the low side; `lower-is-better` (cost, errors, churn)
puts it on the high side. Unset ⇒ the semantic type decides (signed measures read as
higher-is-better, temperatures run warm-high).
props.name: polarity

props.doc: The T2 semantic type string (e.g., "Amount", "Score", "Month")
props.name: semanticType

props.doc: Explicit ordinal ordering. E.g., ["Low", "Medium", "High"]
props.name: sortOrder

props.doc: Unit or currency code. E.g., "USD", "°C", "kg"
props.name: unit

TargetDetailsOptions.doc: Pointer acquisition that snaps to a nearby mark instead of requiring a direct hit.

props.doc:
Distance in px from an axis title to the plot-side edge it labels.
Realization maps this to native title padding or, for a flat y title,
to its offset above the plot.
props.name: axisTitleGap

props.doc:
Where a still-needed axis title sits. `flatAboveAxis` lays it straight
at the head of its own ruler, beside the values it names.
props.name: axisTitlePlacement

props.doc:
`whenAmbiguous` asks the same question of each axis: `Jan Feb Mar` names
its own kind and needs no title over it, `26 20 14` names nothing until
one is written. Ranks and binned ranges count as numbers.
`omit` moves required titles and declared units to the end of the
subtitle rather than relying on the author's prose to name the axes.
props.name: axisTitles

props.doc:
Number compaction (1,250,000 → 1.25M). The theme says whether, how and where; the field
says whether it may be — by its semantic type (`types`) and its unit (a value already in
millions, `Population (m)`, is never compacted again). Unset, `thousands: "suffix"`
compacts value labels value by value, as before; otherwise nothing is compacted.
props.name: compact

props.doc: Where: measure-axis ticks, value labels, or both (default). Tooltips always print the full value.
props.name: on

props.doc: `scale` (default): one unit for a whole ruler or label set, from its largest value; `value`: each its own.
props.name: per

props.doc: `auto` (the default once `compact` is stated) compacts where the largest value reaches `threshold`.
props.name: show

props.doc: `short` k/M/B/T (default), `upper` K/M/B/T (BI), `lower` k/m/b/t, `editorial` k/m/bn/tn, `si` k/M/G/T.
props.name: style

props.doc: The least largest value that is compacted. Default 10,000.
props.name: threshold

props.doc: The semantic types (or families) compacted. Default Amount, Price, Profit, Count, Number, Quantity.
props.name: types

ThemeChartDefaults.doc:
The one block that is allowed to name a chart type.

Everything else at level 1 is a policy the compiler binds to whatever chart
it is handed. This is different in kind: it is the house's list of settings
for charts it has an opinion about — the Times puts a dot on every reading
of a line, and a bump chart it prints is never smoothed. Those are not
consequences of a design language, they are house rules, and there is no
honest way to derive them from ink and type.

Keyed by chart type id, or `*` for every chart. Values are chart-property
keys the template already declares. It is a *default*: anything the caller
set explicitly wins, and a key the template does not offer is reported and
dropped. So is a key that changes how the data is read rather than how the
chart looks: axis type, zero baseline, log scale, transform, encoding actions.

ThemeCompileDefaults.doc:
Compiler settings the house prefers — the size it draws at, how far a chart
may stretch, how much air a facet gets. These are not style: they decide how
much room the chart has before a single colour is chosen, which is why they
cannot be applied after the fact like ink.

Three levels, in order: what the caller put in the chart spec, then this,
then flint's own defaults. A house sets the middle one.

props.doc: Whether to add tooltips to the chart (default: false)
props.name: addTooltips

props.doc: The range's spread either side of its centre, as a ratio: unset, the stretch allowed.
props.name: aspectTolerance

props.doc:
Whether to auto-wrap column-only facets into a 2D grid.

When `true` (default), `computeFacetGrid` considers wrapping N
column facets into multiple rows, choosing the layout whose
overall aspect ratio best matches the canvas AR.

When `false`, column-only facets stay in a single row (capped
at the maximum that fits the canvas budget). Useful for small
multiples that should always be side-by-side.
props.name: autoFacetWrap

props.doc:
Whether a plot with one banded axis leans back where its bands, with the labels it cannot
drop, put it outside the shapes a chart of its base takes on its own (default true). That
range runs from the base with its height stretched to the base with its width stretched
(at least 1.25× either side); where it cannot be reached readably, a range half as wide
again is aimed for instead.
props.name: bandBalance

props.doc:
Blend between the scaled base band and the available span per item.

 baseSpanStep = baseSpan / N
 capacityStep = availableCapacity / N
 preferredStep = baseSpanStep > baseStep
     ? baseStep × (1 − fit) + capacityStep × fit
     : baseStep

`0` gives fixed-step behavior (Vega-Lite); `1` aims toward the available
canvas capacity on sparse axes (ECharts, Chart.js, Plotly). The selected
pitch then passes through normal elastic stretch/compression. Two-banded
cell grids bypass this policy. Default: 0.
props.name: bandStepFit

props.doc: Explicit X-axis capacity for sparse band fitting. Internal assembler bridge.
props.name: bandStepFitCapacityX

props.doc: Explicit Y-axis capacity for sparse band fitting. Internal assembler bridge.
props.name: bandStepFitCapacityY

props.doc:
Backend-native base font size (px) for axis **tick labels**, at a 300px
reference canvas. The core scales it subtly with canvas size and uses it
as the ceiling of the shrink→rotate→cap ladder, so a chart never renders
ticks below its backend's native scale on a comfortable canvas.

Learned from each renderer's defaults:
  - Vega-Lite: 10   - ECharts: 12   - Chart.js: 12   - Plotly: 12

Default: 10.
props.name: baseLabelFontSize

props.doc:
Backend-native base font size (px) for **headers** (axis titles, legend,
chart title), at a 300px reference canvas. Scaled subtly with canvas size
(grows up to +4 on large canvases, shrinks toward the base in small
multiples) so headers stay proportionate to the chart.

Learned from each renderer's defaults:
  - Vega-Lite: 11   - ECharts: 12   - Chart.js: 12   - Plotly: 14

Default: 11.
props.name: baseTitleFontSize

props.doc:
What the layout does when the chart will not read well in its canvas: the title, keys, labels
and chrome taking the chart area's room, the drawing overflowing its box past legibility, or
stretched out of its box's shape. `'auto'` (the default) lays such a chart out again — each part
given a box from the canvas and fitted to it (keys on the edge with room, their names wrapped;
the title set down to fit), then, where that is not enough, cheap treatments one at a time — and
keeps the cheapest that reads well. A chart that reads well as planned is never changed.
`'off'` lays every chart out as planned.
props.name: canvasFit

props.doc:
Whether the canvas fit, once it has settled what is around the chart, lays the plot out once
more in the room the box leaves it — kept only where the chart reads better for it (default true).
props.name: canvasRefit

props.doc: Internal: the treatment a canvas-fit pass lays the chart out under.
props.name: canvasTreatment

props.doc:
How far a grid's cells grow past their reading target (28 px) toward the size that fills the
base, from 0 (not at all, the default) to 1 (to twice the target at most). Set from a house's
`layout.bandStepFit`.
props.name: cellGrowth

props.doc:
Gas-pressure tuning for continuous axes (default: scatter-plot settings).
- A single number overrides markCrossSection (σ) for both axes.
- An object allows per-axis σ plus optional elasticity / maxStretch:
  `{ x: 100, y: 0, elasticity: 0.7, maxStretch: 2 }`
  x/y = 0 means "don't stretch this axis".
  Useful for line/area charts where horizontal crowding matters
  far more than vertical.
props.name: continuousMarkCrossSection

props.doc: Per-axis stretch elasticity (default: 0.3). Higher → more responsive.
props.name: elasticity

props.doc: Per-axis stretch cap (default: 1.5).
props.name: maxStretch

props.doc:
Which axis uses series-count-based pressure instead of pixel counting.
- 'x' or 'y': that axis uses nSeries × σ / dim for pressure.
- 'auto': auto-detect — in 2D (both continuous), defaults to 'y';
  in 1D (one continuous + one discrete), uses the continuous axis.
The σ for the series axis is used directly (not sqrt'd) since series
count is inherently 1D.
props.name: seriesCountAxis

props.doc:
Base pixels per discrete category at a 300px baseline canvas.
Scaled proportionally with canvas size by the core layout engine.
The final default step size is:

  defaultStepSize = defaultBandSize × max(1, canvasSize/300)

Backends set this to match their native bar/band rendering:
  - VL:  ~20 (VL uses width:{step:N} which auto-sizes the plot area)
  - EC:  ~20 (ECharts adds generous grid margins)
  - CJS: ~30 (Chart.js fills the canvas; wider bands look more native)

Templates can override via paramOverrides for chart types that need
more space per band (e.g. jitter: 40, funnel: 50, sankey: 60).

Default: 20.
props.name: defaultBandSize

props.doc: Power-law exponent for discrete axis stretch (default: 0.5)
props.name: elasticity

props.doc:
Resistance to aspect-ratio distortion when faceting.

When faceting divides one dimension (e.g. width by column count),
the subplot aspect ratio drifts away from the single-plot ratio.
Line and area charts are very sensitive to this because their
visual signal is encoded in slopes and curve shapes.

This parameter partially compensates by shrinking the undivided
dimension so the panel aspect ratio stays closer to the original:

  arDrift = facetedAR / baseAR          (< 1 when panel is narrower)
  correctedDim = dim × arDrift ^ resistance

- 0 (default): no correction — current behavior.
- 0.3–0.5: moderate resistance (recommended for line / area).
- 1: fully preserve the single-plot aspect ratio.
props.name: facetAspectRatioResistance

props.doc:
Explicit number of facet COLUMNS for a column-wrapped facet, overriding
the auto-computed wrap. When set (≥ 1) the layout uses this many columns
(clamped to the distinct column count) and wraps the remaining panels
into as many rows as needed. Surfaced to hosts as the `facetColumns`
chart property so users can dial the wrap in interactively; undefined =
auto (fill the width).
props.name: facetColumns

props.doc: Power-law exponent for facet subplot stretch — lower = more conservative (default: 0.3)
props.name: facetElasticity

props.doc:
Fixed overhead in px for axis labels, titles, legend, etc.
Subtracted once from the total canvas budget (not per-panel).
Each backend sets its own default; core uses { width: 0, height: 0 }.
props.name: facetFixedPadding

props.doc:
Gap in px between adjacent facet panels (spacing, headers).
Used directly by the core layout engine to compute subplot sizes
and max canvas dimensions.
Each backend sets its own value (VL ≈ 10, ECharts ≈ 14); core uses 0.
props.name: facetGap

props.doc: The gap between facet columns and between facet rows the panels are laid out for, where it differs from `facetGap`; set by the plan.
props.name: facetGapColumn

props.doc:
When a discrete axis is **grouped** (dodged lanes within each category
band), by default the band's elastic stretch target is the *per-item*
step — so a category holding N lanes is only sized as if it held one.
For thin marks (grouped bars) that's fine: 4 lanes share a ~66px band
comfortably. But wide marks — a box-and-whisker glyph — need real room
per lane, and the per-item target leaves grouped boxplots compressed on
an otherwise roomy canvas.

When set, the grouped band instead targets `itemsPerGroup × step`, so
the category band stretches to give each lane its full width (still
bounded by `maxBandSize × itemsPerGroup` and the canvas budget). Scoped
to templates whose grouped glyph is wide (boxplot); left off for bars so
their tuned grouped spacing does not change.
props.name: groupBandFillsLanes

props.doc:
The smallest band step (per group where bars are grouped) the value labels need on each axis,
which the plan has checked the canvas can hold. Internal: the plan sets it when it widens the
bands for their labels.
props.name: labelStep

props.doc:
Set by the interactive renderer when a viewport will change the rows in view:
value labels are built for any window that could print them, and this signal
decides whether they show.
props.name: liveLayoutSignal

props.doc:
When true, continuous X and Y axes stretch together using the
larger of the two per-axis stretch factors. This preserves the
aspect ratio of the data space. (default: false — axes stretch
independently based on their own density.)
props.name: maintainContinuousAxisRatio

props.doc:
Maximum pixels per discrete category at a 300px baseline canvas,
scaled proportionally with canvas size (like {@link defaultBandSize}).

This is the **sparse-expansion ceiling**. When few categories share a
wide plot, each band grows to fill the available width but never past
`maxBandSize`, so one or two bars can't balloon to the whole canvas.
The band is thus clamped to `[minStep, maxBandSize]`:

  step = clamp(availableWidth / N, minStep, maxBandSize)

Backends set this to match their native sparse-bar rendering:
  - VL:  = defaultBandSize (VL's step-based sizing doesn't fill a container)
  - EC / CJS / Plotly: much larger (these fill their plot area natively)

Defaults to {@link defaultBandSize} (no expansion beyond the base band).
props.name: maxBandSize

props.doc: Maximum number of distinct color values before overflow truncation (default: 24)
props.name: maxColorValues

props.doc:
Default maximum stretch multiplier used when the spec provides no
explicit `canvasSize` ceiling (default: 2).

This is a **unified** budget: the combined stretch from facet
layout AND discrete/banded axis sizing must stay within this
factor.  For example, with maxStretch=2 and a 400px base,
the total chart width never exceeds 800px regardless of how
many facet columns or discrete axis items there are.

When `chart_spec.canvasSize` IS set, the per-dimension caps
`maxStretchX`/`maxStretchY` are derived from `canvasSize / baseSize`
instead and this scalar is ignored.
props.name: maxStretch

props.doc:
Resolved per-dimension stretch cap for the X (width) axis.

Normally derived by the assembler from `canvasSize / baseSize`
(or `maxStretch` when no ceiling is set). Callers rarely set this
directly. Falls back to `maxStretch` when absent.
props.name: maxStretchX

props.doc:
Resolved per-dimension stretch cap for the Y (height) axis.

Normally derived by the assembler from `canvasSize / baseSize`
(or `maxStretch` when no ceiling is set). Callers rarely set this
directly. Falls back to `maxStretch` when absent.
props.name: maxStretchY

props.doc:
Chart-specific **floor** on the per-category band step (at a 300px
baseline canvas), which a house's `layout.bandStep` may grow but not
undercut. Ordinary charts have no such floor: a compact house is right
to print thin bars. But a few chart types are only legible above a
minimum band width regardless of house — a slopegraph draws its whole
meaning from the angle of two columns, and a house that packs them 46px
apart turns every slope near-vertical and leaves no room for the end
labels. Such a template states the width its read needs here, and the
house is held to it as a minimum while still free to spread wider.

Unset for most templates (no floor). Set via paramOverrides.
props.name: minBandStep

props.doc:
The smallest axis tick label (px) the shrink ladder may reach, as small multiples
shrink their plots. A themed chart takes its theme's `type.minSize`. Default: 6.
props.name: minLabelFontSize

props.doc: Minimum pixels per discrete axis item (default: 6)
props.name: minStep

props.doc: Minimum facet subplot size in px (default: 60)
props.name: minSubplotSize

props.doc:
Internal: the names down y stand on their own line above each bar. The y band starts at
`scale` times the house band, never under `scale` times the least step nor `minStep` — a
name's line, its bar and the air between — by the same stretch.
props.name: rowNamesAbove

props.doc:
Fraction of each step reserved for inter-category padding (0–1).
VL pads *inside* the step (band = step × (1 − padding)), so this
value should match VL's paddingInner.  ECharts pads *outside* the
band, so the layout engine passes this through so ECharts can
compute barWidth = step × (1 − stepPadding) explicitly.

Default: 0.1 (matching VL's default band paddingInner).
props.name: stepPadding

props.doc: The centre of that range, as width over height: unset, the base's.
props.name: targetAspect

props.doc:
Target aspect ratio for a single band (step height ÷ step width).

When a banded (discrete) axis is opposite a continuous axis, each
band has a natural AR = continuousAxisSize / stepSize.  If that
exceeds the target, the continuous axis is shrunk via a log-space
blend so bands don't become excessively tall/wide.

- `undefined` / 0: no band-AR correction.
- Typical values: 8–15 (VL default ≈ 10, ECharts ≈ 12).

Only affects charts with exactly one banded axis and one
continuous axis (e.g. bar, lollipop).  Has no effect on
scatter, line, or fully-banded charts.
props.name: targetBandAR

props.doc: Attach the theme's resolved decisions to the spec as `_theme.decisions`, for tools that inspect them. Default: false.
props.name: themeDecisions

props.doc:
Where a label printed inside a bar sits along it: at the value `end` (default), at the bar's
`start` (its base, so the numbers read as one column), or in the `middle`.
props.name: anchor

props.doc:
When some bars are too short to hold their label inside: `perMark` (default) prints just those
past their end; `allOutside` prints every label past its bar's end, so they read alike.
props.name: fallback

props.doc: The contrast (x:1) a label printed on a mark keeps with it under `contrastWithMark`; default 3.
props.name: minContrast

props.doc: Which end of its frame it sits at. Default `start`. Rules and bands span the frame.
props.name: align

props.doc: The image's text alternative.
props.name: alt

props.doc: The earlier corner placement, read by `mastheadTab`, `headerRule` and `footerRule`.
props.name: anchor

props.doc: Where it sits. Defaults: `canvasTop` for rules, bands and tabs; `aboveTitle` for text and images.
props.name: at

props.doc: What it is aligned to or spans. Defaults: `canvas` for a rule or band on the edge, else `content`.
props.name: frame

props.doc: px. A rule's weight, a band's or tab's or image's height.
props.name: height

props.doc: Where the item links to, when it is clicked.
props.name: href

props.doc:
`rule` — a line across its frame; `band` — a filled strip across its frame; `tab` — a short
block (the Economist's red tab); `text` — a wordmark or credit; `image` — a logo, from inline
`svg` or an image `src`. `mastheadTab`, `headerRule` and `footerRule` are the earlier names:
a tab above the title at the content's start, a rule below the title across the block, and a
rule below the plot.
props.name: kind

props.doc: An image URL or data URI for an `image` item.
props.name: src

props.doc: Inline SVG markup for an `image` item.
props.name: svg

props.doc: The words of a `text` item, set in `type` (else the deck's type).
props.name: text

props.doc: px. A tab's or image's width; a rule or band spans its frame unless given one.
props.name: width

ThemeGeometry.doc:
Geometry the house states once and every chart built from that shape reads.

Measured against the theme lab: `line.width`, `point.presence` and
`point.size` all split inside a replicated cluster — one chart, many
languages, different answers — so they are house decisions and belong here.
`point.fill` did not split, which is why nothing here asks a house to state it.

There is deliberately no per-chart-type sibling to this block. The lab was
asked for one and refused: of the twelve (house, chart type) groups holding
more than one chart, eight disagree with themselves, so a rule keyed by chart
type could not have carried them anyway. What the disagreements track is
series count and faceting — NYT, the Economist and Power BI all thin their
line to exactly 2px for the four-series chart and run 2.2–2.5px for a lone
one, and Power BI drops its dots only on the sixteen-panel facet. Those are
`variants`, over signals the compiler already resolves, and a variant may
carry a `geometry` block.

ThemeGuard.doc: A predicate over signals the compiler already resolves. Deliberately closed.

props.doc:
Inks for one family of marks, keyed by mark: `line`, `area`, `bar` (bars and cells),
`arc` (pies and donuts) or `point`. A chart whose series are drawn by one family takes that
family's `single` and `categorical` in place of the general ones; a chart mixing families
(bars with a line) keeps the general set, so a series has one colour throughout.
props.name: byMark

props.doc:
A set written for an exact number of series, keyed by that number (`{ 2: [...], 3: [...] }`).
A chart with that many series takes its set instead of the first inks of `categorical`. A
chart with more series than `categorical` names may also reach a larger set here, the way it
reaches `categoricalExtended`. One series keeps `single`.
props.name: categoricalByCount

props.doc:
A larger indexed set the house reaches for when a chart has more
series than its core {@link categorical } palette can name, in the
spirit of Tableau's 10→20 step. The core set carries the house's
identity at low cardinality (a handful of well-known inks); the
extended set trades a little of that identity for the capacity to
keep every series distinct up to its length. Grounding picks the
smallest set whose length covers the series count; past the extended
set's length the {@link overflow } ink takes the tail.

Must contain the core set's inks as a prefix is *not* required — but
ordering the shared hues first keeps a chart's colours stable as it
grows. Unset ⇒ the house has only its core palette.
props.name: categoricalExtended

props.doc:
The ink each categorical entry takes when it is *written* rather than filled — a series
name at a line's end, a value in the series' colour. Parallel to {@link categorical } (then
{@link categoricalExtended }): entry *i* is the text variant of ink *i*. Where a house gives
none, a series ink too light to read on the surface is darkened in its own hue until it
reaches 3:1.
props.name: categoricalText

props.doc:
The least contrast a series ink keeps against the plot surface. A fill below `fill`
(default 1.25:1) is drawn with a 1px edge in a darker shade of its hue; a line below
`stroke` (default 1.6:1) is darkened in its hue until it passes. Inks that pass are
untouched.
props.name: minContrast

props.doc:
The ramp for ordered series (Gold, Silver, Bronze; Strongly agree … Strongly disagree), its
stops listed in the order the categories take them. Unset ⇒ ordered series sample
`sequential`.
props.name: ordinal

props.doc:
Past the last ink, start the palette again instead of folding the rest into the overflow
ink: for houses whose guide says colours repeat after the *n*th series.
props.name: repeat

props.doc:
Inks for values that play a role, whatever their position: `other` (Other, Others, Rest of
world …), `total` (Total, Grand total) and `missing` (Missing, Unknown, No data, N/A …).
A value with a role takes its ink and no other series in the chart wears it. `other` is
also the overflow ink when the house names none. Colours for particular values (a party,
an asset class) belong to the chart: the field annotation `colors`, which wins over these.
props.name: roles

props.doc:
A nominal series whose order the chart declares (the field annotation's `sortOrder`):
`ramp` reads it as ordered and samples the ordinal ramp; `categorical` (default) keeps
distinct hues. A sequence Flint infers on its own (months, compass points) is not
declared and keeps distinct hues.
props.name: ordered

props.doc:
How a signed series is coloured. Applies only when the coloured field itself carries
the sign: a continuous colour whose values cross zero, or categories that split by
sign (increase / decrease, regions netting a gain or a loss). A measure on an axis
that dips below zero leaves the series' colour to the ordinal and categorical rules.
props.name: signed

props.doc: The ink the presence ordinal scales against.
props.name: structure

props.doc:
The stem of a lollipop, the bridge of a dumbbell. It borrows `rule`
where the house says nothing, but the two are not the same job: a
gridline is read *through*, so it sits at the bottom of the ordinal,
while a connector is part of the mark and has to hold its shape at
a hairline's width. A house whose gridlines are already pale has no
room left below them, and states this ink instead.
props.name: connector

props.doc:
The zero line, when the house makes it more than one gridline among
the rest. The Economist strokes zero in its signature red so every
length is read from a line the eye cannot miss. It borrows `rule`
(then `axis`) where the house says nothing, so a house that draws an
ordinary zero needs to state nothing.
props.name: zero

props.doc: Paint for the exterior of a contiguous semantic selection.
props.name: selectionBoundary

props.doc: Set to zero to disable the contrast halo.
props.name: haloWidth

ThemeLabelFit.doc: The thresholds category names are set against (`labels.fit`).

props.doc: Space two straight names keep between them, in em. Default half an em, at least 6px.
props.name: gap

props.doc: Characters a cut name keeps before its ellipsis; a cut that keeps fewer is not taken. Default 4.
props.name: minChars

props.doc: The widest a row name down y runs before it wraps or is cut: px, or a share of the chart's width. Default a quarter of it, at least 180px.
props.name: rowLimit

props.doc: The widest a turned name runs before it is cut: px, or a share of the plot's height (`"40%"`, the default).
props.name: turnedLimit

props.doc: The thresholds the names are set against; each has a default.
props.name: fit

props.doc:
The path category names along x take when they do not stand flat and whole. Names that fit
are always flat — a theme never forces a turn. Leave it unset for the general path:
- a row of names: `["wrap", "rotate90"]`;
- a sequence that explains itself (times, dates, months, years, decades, ranks, by semantic
  type): `["wrap", "skip", "rotate90"]`.
Add `"rotate45"` before `"rotate90"` where the house turns labels 45°. Steps: `wrap` (two
lines, or one in wider bands), `skip` (only the round values, sequences only), `rotate45`,
`rotate90`. Trimming is not a step: any step may trim its names (an ellipsis at the band or
at `fit.turnedLimit`) unless `truncation` is `"never"`. The path's order binds; within it,
every step is weighed at every size down to the floor and the cheapest taken. A chart can
state its own path in `chartProperties.labelOverflow`.
props.name: overflow

props.doc:
Where the names of horizontal bars stand. `beside` (the default): down the y axis, left of the
bars. `above`: each on its own line over its bar, the full width of the chart theirs — the
bands take twice their room, by the same stretch, and where the canvas cannot hold that the
names stand beside. `auto`: above only where, beside, a name would be cut or wrapped. One bar
to a band only: grouped bars and small multiples keep their names beside.
props.name: rowNames

props.doc:
How strongly category pitch follows the available discrete-axis span.
  On sparse one-banded axes, `0` preserves `bandStep`, `1` fills the span,
  and intermediate values linearly blend the two. Under pressure normal
  elasticity applies to `bandStep`. A grid's cells (both axes banded) are not bars: they keep
  their reading target, and grow past it toward the size that fills the base by this share, to
  twice the target at most.
props.name: bandStepFit

props.doc:
Air around the plot: the canvas padding, and a key's gap to the plot (0.8, 1 or 1.4 em of its
labels, unless `legend.gaps.plot` says). Not the ruler's gradations — those are `tickDensity`.
props.name: density

props.doc: The vertical gap between the headline and its deck (subtitle).
props.name: deckGap

props.doc:
The edge the title block starts from: `content` (default) — the canvas inside its margin,
past the category labels; `plot` — the plot's own left edge, so the headline lines up with
the start of the x axis.
props.name: frame

props.doc:
The vertical gap between the title block and the chart below it — a
house's whitespace personality reaching the headline. `tight` packs
the chart up under the title (a dense figure, a dashboard tile);
`loose` gives an action title room to breathe (a slide exhibit). Keys above the plot join
the block: the title stands an em over them (`legend.gaps.title`), and this gap
stands below them.
props.name: gap

props.doc: Place the semantic title above the chart or as a caption below it.
props.name: position

props.doc: Where keys stand along their edge: from its start, centred, at its end, or spread across it.
props.name: align

props.doc: Several keys above or below the plot: side by side, or one above another. A preference: it gives way where the keys would overflow.
props.name: arrangement

props.doc:
Names at the line ends also say where each line ends — "Japan 84.5" — in the value labels'
number format. They follow the rows the chart draws, so a chart whose rows are replaced
(re-indexed, filtered) keeps its names honest.
props.name: endValue

props.doc:
The air around keys, in em of their labels — so it keeps its proportion to the type — and
eased smoothly with the plot's size (0.7 on a small tile to 1.3 on a large chart).
`title`: the title block to keys standing under it; `stack`: between keys one above another;
`row`: between keys side by side, and keys one above another beside the plot; `plot`: a key to
the plot. Unset: the header grouped by its gaps — 0.6 em for `stack`, an em for `title`, 2.25 em
for `row`; an em for `plot`, by `layout.density`.
props.name: gaps

props.doc:
The most entries a key to *values* may spend. A legend that names ten
bubble sizes is a table, not a key. Unset, a size key lists round values
as its edge has room for — one for every 80 px of the plot's side it
stands on, from three to five — each symbol clearly larger than the last.
props.name: maxSwatches

props.doc: The legend restates the categorical axis — delete it.
props.name: suppressWhenAxisNames

props.doc: The legend restates a number already printed in every mark — delete it.
props.name: suppressWhenValuesPrinted

props.doc:
The symbol beside each name in a key to categories: `auto` (default) takes it from the mark —
a square for bars, a stroke for lines, the dot's own shape for points; `square`, `circle` or
`line` (a short stroke) draw that symbol for every mark. A key whose entries are shapes (a
shape channel) or sizes keeps its own symbols. Vega-Lite only.
props.name: swatch

props.doc:
Whether a key carries its field's name. `always`; or `whenAmbiguous` (the default), which
leaves it off only on proof the reader does not need it: the headline, deck or an axis on the
same field already names it, the chart makes the key itself, or every value proves one closed
kind (months, years, countries…) under a field name that says no more. A semantic type is not
proof. An author who wants no title says so on the encoding. `omit` is read as `whenAmbiguous`.
props.name: title

props.doc: A key's title above its entries, or before them on their line, above or below the plot. A preference.
props.name: titlePosition

props.doc: Wedge order, start angle and hole (`geometry.arc`).
props.name: arc

props.doc: The line along the top of each area (`geometry.area.edge`), in the area's own ink; never an outline on other marks.
props.name: areaEdge

props.doc: The least length, px, of a non-zero bar (`geometry.band.minLength`).
props.name: barMinLength

props.doc: How opaque a bar's fill is (`geometry.band.opacity`), 0–1; areas keep `fillOpacity`.
props.name: barOpacity

props.doc:
The weight of a connector that runs between two marks — a dumbbell's
bridge. This one is not redundant: the *distance* it draws is the
reading, and a hairline asks the eye to measure a gap it can barely
see. It keeps structure's ink and takes a mark's weight.

Where the house says nothing, a bridge is drawn at the weight the
house gives its lines: it is a mark, so it takes a mark's weight.
props.name: spanWeight

props.doc:
The weight of a connector that runs from a mark to the baseline — a
lollipop's stem. It restates nothing: the dot's position already
carries the value and the stem only leads the eye down to the axis,
so it is drawn as structure.
props.name: weight

props.doc:
How far the *value* end of a bar is rounded, in px — the top of a
column, the right of a horizontal bar — and, on a wedge, its corners.
Only the value end of a bar moves; the baseline stays a clean edge, so a
stack still reads as one column. A house that says nothing keeps square
corners; a friendlier, less clinical house rounds them.
props.name: cornerRadius

props.doc: Gradient fills: an area that fades to its baseline, a wash under each line.
props.name: gradient

props.doc: How a group of bars shares its step (`geometry.band.group`).
props.name: group

props.doc: `series` draws each mark's border in its own series ink, at full strength.
props.name: outline

props.doc:
Which lines keep the dots (M5): `countable` (default) — lines of up to 12 readings; `all` —
every line, the dots shrinking to fit; `sparse` — only where readings stand 20px apart or more.
props.name: density

props.doc:
A ring in the plot's surface colour around each dot, so dots that overlap, or sit on a line,
stay countable. A line's dots get one wherever lines can cross unless this says `omit`; a
scatter's dots get one only where it is declared. An `outline` takes its place (a dot has
one stroke). A halo and an opacity below 1 are not combined: ringed dots are solid.
props.name: halo

props.doc:
The ink of a line's vertex dots: the series' own ink (the default), the house's text ink
(dark dots on coloured lines), or a colour the house names. A scatter's dots are the
series and always take its ink.
props.name: ink

props.doc: How opaque a dot is, 0–1; unset, the renderer's own.
props.name: opacity

props.doc:
Whether a *line* carries a dot at each of its vertices. This is a
question about lines, not about dots: a scatter's dots are drawn
because the chart is a scatter, and no house presence turns them off.
props.name: presence

props.doc:
How big a supporting vertex is, as an area in px². A radar vertex or
a sampled point on a connected shape confirms the path's position;
it is not the primary mark and must not obscure that path or its
grid. Defaults to the smaller of `size` and 25px².
props.name: secondarySize

props.doc: The glyph every dot is drawn as; see {@link PointShape}.
props.name: shape

props.doc:
How big a primary dot this house draws, as an area in px² — the way
the renderer states a point's size and the way the size channel is
read. This covers marks whose point is itself the reading: a scatter,
a dot plot, or the ends of a dumbbell.

Where the house says nothing the renderer's default stands. The
layout remains free to shrink it when the plot runs short of room.
props.name: size

props.doc:
A wedge sits in no band, so how far apart neighbouring wedges stand is
its own question. A house may rule its stacked bars with a half-pixel
hairline and still want a clean cut between the pieces of a pie: two
arcs of the same size at different orientations are hard enough to
compare without also having to find where one ends. Where the house
says nothing, wedges are held apart the way its bars are.

`rule` paints the shared edge in the separator's ink, which reads as a
gap of constant width. `pad` swings the wedges apart instead, so the
gap opens at the rim and closes to nothing at the centre.
props.name: slice

props.doc:
How the `texture` channel is drawn on filled marks (bars, wedges, areas): `vary` (default)
gives each series its own pattern — diagonal, the other diagonal, horizontal, vertical, cross,
dots — so series differ without colour; `hatch` gives every series the same diagonal hatch in
its own ink. `patterns` names the house's own sequence instead, in palette order (`solid`
leaves that series a flat fill). The lines are a darker shade of the fill (`ink: "darker"`) or white.
props.name: texture

props.doc:
How far apart the cells of a grid stand — a heatmap, a calendar, a
matrix. A cell is not a bar: it has no band to give back, its two
neighbours are on two axes, and its colour is the reading, so a gap
between cells has to be cut out of the shape the way a wedge's is.

Whether to cut at all is a real difference between houses and not a
detail. Flush cells read as a continuous field — the eye follows the
gradient across a row and sees a season. Cut cells read as a table of
separate readings, which is what a house wants when it prints the number
inside each one. Where the house says nothing, cells are held apart the
way its bars are.

The gap is painted, not spaced, and it takes the surface unless the
house asks for structure: on a grid whose colour *is* the value, an edge
in any other ink reads as data.
props.name: tile

ThemeSource.doc:
The source line (S1). The chart says what the source is (`chart_spec.source`); the house says how
it reads: a lead-in, where it sits, a rule above it, a credit of its own. Set in `type.footnote`.

props.doc: Which end of the frame the line sits at; default `start`.
props.name: align

props.doc:
The house's own credit: `inline` after the source (with `separator`), at the frame's other
`end`, or on the `nextLine`.
props.name: credit

props.doc:
A logo in place of the credit's words, at the frame's other end, level with the source
(`placement: "end"` only; `text` stays its alternative text): inline `svg` or a `src` URL
or data URI (PNG works), drawn `width`×`height` px.
props.name: image

props.doc: `content` (default): inside the margin, with the headline; `canvas`: the graphic's outer edges.
props.name: frame

props.doc: px between the chart and the source line (or its rule); default 8.
props.name: gap

props.doc: The words before the source; default `"Source:"`, `""` for none.
props.name: leadIn

props.doc: The lead-in's weight, slope and case, where they differ from the source's.
props.name: leadInWeight

props.doc: A rule across the frame above the source line.
props.name: rule

props.doc: `whenGiven` (default) draws the chart's source; `never` leaves it to the host page.
props.name: show

ThemeSpec.doc:
Level 1. One JSON document per design language.

Every field is optional, including the ink and the type. A house that states
nothing is not an error — it is the neutral house, and grounding it yields
Flint's own defaults. That matters beyond tidiness: it is what lets the
compiler reason about a chart's design (can it carry value labels? at this
density?) when the caller named no house at all, without having to invent a
second, parallel set of rules for the untheme'd case.

props.doc:
Start from a theme Flint ships, then override only the fields this
specification states. Nested objects merge; arrays and scalar values
replace the preset value.
props.name: extends

props.doc: How a chart's source line is drawn, when the chart gives one (`chart_spec.source`).
props.name: source

props.doc: The axis the chart is indexed by, wherever it is drawn.
props.name: categorical

props.doc:
What the axis lines are where the value scale floats — does not start at zero, as a line
or scatter at 45–90 does. `omit`: the line along the floor is a base, and a base there
would claim a zero the chart does not have, so it is not drawn; the value grid marks the
floor where a tick stands, and the line's ticks go with it. `keep`: the lines frame the
window, wherever it starts. `rangeFrame`: the lines span only the data, set off from the
plot (Tufte's range frame), so the frame stays and says where the data runs. Unset, a
house that rules its value axis keeps the frame; one that grids its values instead omits
the line. Bars and areas start at zero, so a floor under them is always a base.
`rangeFrame` is drawn by Vega-Lite only.
props.name: floating

props.doc: The axis values are read off, wherever it is drawn.
props.name: measure

props.doc:
The axis drawn along the bottom or top (x), whatever it carries: its settings override
the role's (AX1). A house that styles its axes by side — a 2px rule along the bottom on
every chart — states it here rather than by role.
props.name: x

props.doc: The axis drawn up the left or right (y), whatever it carries; overrides the role's.
props.name: y

props.doc: The rule the marks stand on (A7): a presence, or one with its own weight, dash and ink.
props.name: baseline

props.doc: This rule's own ink, in place of the role's (`ink.structure.grid`, `.zero`, `.axis`); the presence still tones it.
props.name: color
